title: Prakas on Debt Securities Offering to Qualified Investors
text:
(Unofficial Translation)
KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA
Securities and Exchange

PRAKAS
on
DEBT SECURITIES OFFERING TO QUALIFIED INVESTORS
    
Deputy Prime Minister
Minister of Economy and Finance
and the Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Cambodia
- Having seen the Constitution of the Kingdom of Cambodia;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kret No. NS/RKT/0918/925 on 06 September 2018 on the
Appointment of the Royal Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No. NS/RKM/0618/012 on 28 June 2018 promulgating
the Law on the Organizing and Functioning of the Council of Ministers;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No. NS/RKM/0196/18 on 24 January 1996
promulgating the Law on the Establishment of the Ministry of Economy and Finance;
- Having seen the Preah Reach Kram No. NS/RKM/1007/028 on 19 October 2007
promulgating the Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities;
- Having seen the Anukret No. 97/ANKR/BK on 23 July 2008 on the Conduct and
Organization of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Cambodia;
- Having seen the Anukret No. 54/ANKR/BK on 08 April 2009 on the Implementation of
the Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities;
- Having seen the Prakas No. 009/17 SECC/PrK on 17 August 2017 on Public Offering of
Debt Securities;
- Having seen the Prakas No. 007/18 SECC/Prk on 30 October 2018 on Corporate
Disclosure;
- Having seen the Prakas No. 005/16 SECC/PrK on 17 August 2016 on Qualified Investors
in the Securities Sector;
- Having seen the approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Cambodia in
plenary meeting on 23 April 2020

HEREBY DECIDE
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISION
Article 1– Purpose
The purpose of this Prakas is to supervise the debt securities offering to qualified
investors in effective, efficient, accountable and transparent manner in the Kingdom of
Cambodia.
Article 2-Objective
The objective of this Prakas is to prescribe the requirements, procedure, and the
approval for debt securities offering to qualified investors pursuant to the Law on Issuance
and Trading of Non-government Securities and the ANUKRET on the Implementation of the
Law on Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities and other related regulations.
Article 3– Scope
This Prakas is applicable for debt securities offering in the Kingdom of Cambodia for
qualified investors only. The offered debt securities shall be transferred to qualified investors
only.
Article 4-Definition
Unless the context requires otherwise, the technical terms used in this Prakas have the
meaning defined in this article and the glossary annexed to the Law on the Issuance and
Trading of Non-Government Securities, and that annexed to the ANUKRET on the
Implementation of the Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-government securities and
the Prakas on Public Offering of Debt Securities.
1- Law refers to the Law on the Issuance and Trading of Non-Government Securities.
2- Qualified Investors refers to institutional investors and high net-worth investors
prescribed in the Prakas on Qualified Investors in the Securities Sector who can
participate in the debt securities offering according to this Prakas.
3- Anukret refers to the Sub-degree on the Implementation of the Law on the Issuance
and Trading of Non-Government Securities.
CHAPTER II
REQUIREMENTS FOR DEBT SECURITIES OFFERING
Article 5- Types of Debt Securities to be Offered
The Debt Securities to be offered pursuant to this Prakas refer to the debt securities as
prescribed in Article 3 of the Prakas on Public Offering of Debt Securities.
Article 6- Application for Debt Securities Offering
An entity who intends to make debt securities offering to qualified investors shall
submit application as stipulated in article 10 of this Prakas to seek approval for debt securities
offering to qualified investors and get disclosure document registered at the SECC.
Disclosure document shall contain the information as prescribed in Article 11 of this

2- Having obtained the Board of Directors’ resolution on the debt securities offering to

3- Having historical financial statements and/or consolidated historical financial
statement for the latest 2 (two) financial years which are audited in accordance with the
existing law and regulations enacted in the Kingdom of Cambodia. The applicant may submit
interim financial statements in case the applicant file the application later than 45 (forty five)
days after the end of the quarter.
4- Having obtained prior verification on listing eligibility review on the debt securities
and securities pricing from permitted securities market.
The applicant is encouraged to implement the corporate governance in accordance with
the existing laws and regulations.
Article 8- Requirements for Secured Bond Offering or Guaranteed Bond Offering
In case of issuing secured bond, the applicant shall fulfill the following requirements:
1-Having fulfilled the requirements as prescribed in Article 7 of this Prakas;
2-Having collateral that complied with the following requirements:
- Have the certification issued by relevant competent authorities that the collateral is
free from any lien;
- In case the collateral is real estate or long-term lease agreement, the value of such
collateral shall be determined by valuation company accredited by the SECC;
3-The amount of proceeds received from the debt securities issuance shall not exceed
70 (seventy) per cent of the value of the collateral as at the date of application.
4-The collateral shall be kept under custody of a custodian agent in the securities
sector.
In case of issuing guaranteed bond, the applicant shall fulfill the following
requirements:
1- Having complied with the requirement as prescribed in Article 7 of this Prakas;
2- Having guarantor who is approved by the SECC. And the guarantor shall be rated
by the credit rating agency accredited by the SECC.
Article 9- Debt Securities Offering to Qualified Investors made by Listed Companies
The listed companies having issued equity securities in public and having intention to
apply for debt securities offering to qualified investors shall comply with the requirements
prescribed in Article 7 or Article 8 of this Prakas except point 3 and point 4 in Article 7 of this
Prakas.
The listed companies having issued debt securities and having intention to apply for
debt securities offering to qualified investors, may be exempted from points 3 and point 4 in
Article 7 of this Prakas in case the applicant has submitted the application at least 30 (thirty)
day prior to the maturity date of the issued debt securities.

CHAPTER III
APPROVAL ON DEBT SECURITIES OFFERING TO QUALIFIED INVESTORS
Article 11– Disclosure Document
Disclosure document shall have the minimum contents as follow:
1- Statement on transfer restriction;
2- Summary of disclosure document;
3- Information about the debt securities offering;
4- Information about the use of proceeds;
5- General information about the applicant and its operation;
6-Information about risk factors;
7- Information about corporate governance;
8- Financial information and/or consolidate financial information;
9- Annex.
Disclosure document shall contain the statement saying “All information in the
disclosure document is under the responsibility of the issuer and the entities related to the
preparation of this disclosure document”.

Article 13- Responsibility of Experts
Pursuance to article 9 and article 10 of the Anukret, experts and the related parties who
gave the consent in writing for any statements, report or opinion used in the disclosure
document shall be responsible for such statement, report or opinion.
Article 14-Supplement, Replacement, Confirmation or Clarification Information
The Director General of the SECC is empowered to require the applicant to provide
supplementary, replacement, confirmation or clarification information. The applicant shall
comply with this requirement within 15 (fifteen) working days or any specific time period
determined by the Director General of the SECC from the date of issuing the written
notification. In case the applicant cannot satisfy the above requirement, the Director General
of the SECC may reject the proposal.
Article 15- Approval and Registration of Disclosure Document
The Director General of the SECC shall inform the applicant in writing about approval
and registration of the disclosure document or rejection within 30 (thirty) working days after
receiving the complete documents.
Article 16- Rejection of the Proposal for Debt Securities Offering to Qualified Investors
The Director General of the SECC may reject the proposal for debt securities offering
to qualified investors based on the following reasons:
1- The applicant doesn’t satisfy the requirements as prescribed by the Law, Anukret and
this Prakas;
2- The information or documents submitted to the SECC contain incomplete, false or
misleading information or lack of any material information;
3- The applicant is in the situation leading to termination or bankruptcy;
4- The non-compliance or partial compliance with the court’s decision which requires
the applicant to pay any judgment sum;
5- The applicant or director, CEO, management or the controlling shareholder of the
applicant:
a- Is not a person of good character as prescribed by Article 42 of the Anukret;
b- Has conducted or engaged in any other business in such a way as to cast doubt on
its or his/her competence and soundness of judgment;
c- Has conducted any business appearing deceitful or oppressive or otherwise
improper;
d- Has shown the fact that it or he/she may not be able to act in the best interest of its
clients because of its or his/her reputation, character, financial integrity and reliability;
e- Has shown the fact that it or he/she may not be able to carry out the businesses

CHAPTER IV
DEBT SECURITIES OFFERING TO QUALIFIED INVESTORS
Article 17- Subscription
After obtaining approval and registration of the disclosure document, the subscription of
debt securities can commence within the validity period of the disclosure document that is
prescribed in point 3 of Article 7 of the Anukret. When the subscription is completed, the
issuer shall submit the report on subscription result to the SECC without delay.
The subscription shall be done by qualified investors and conducted through securities
firm licensed by the SECC as prescribed in Article 16 and Article 17 of the Anukret and the
Prakas on Qualified Investors in the Securities Sector. The securities firm shall deposit the
cash received from the subscription into a separate bank account opened with commercial
bank as stipulated in Article 18 of the Anukret. The list of subscribers’ names shall be kept
with the securities registrar.
The subscription form shall be determined by the SECC. Each subscription shall be
considered as completed when subscribers have correctly filled in the subscription form, fully
paid and received receipt issued by the securities firm. The subscribers may not withdraw
amounts paid for the subscription, except for the case stipulated in point 4-b of Article 7 and
point 2 of Article 18 of the Anukret and Article 21, 22 and 23 of this Prakas.
Article 18- Subscription the Remaining Debt Securities
After the end of subscription date, in the case debt securities remain unsubscribed, the
underwriter of the issuer shall subscribe to those remaining debt securities or those as stated
in the underwriting agreement and fully pay the issuer in cash or with other financial
instruments as prescribed by Article 8 of the Anukret by the next working day after the
closing date of the subscription. The issuer shall submit the report on the subscription of the
remaining debt securities to the SECC without delay.
Article 19- Distribution of Debt Securities
The securities firm shall distribute debt securities at the price set in the registered
disclosure document.
The issuer, securities registrar or securities firm shall distribute and dispatch debt
securities to successful subscribers by the next working day after the closing date of
subscription of the debt securities.
Article 20-Debt Securities Deposit at the Depository Operator
After debt securities have been allocated to qualified investors, the issuer shall deposit
all debt securities issued at the securities depository operator approved by the SECC.

Article 22- Announcement on Cancellation of Registered Disclosure Document
The issuer shall immediately notify subscribers about the cancellation of registered
disclosure document directly and/or through any method that got approval from the Director
General of the SECC by specifying the following:
1- Reason of the cancellation of the registered disclosure document;
2- Date of the Decision on the cancellation of the registered disclosure document;
3- Time, place and the method of refund to the subscribers who already paid for the
subscription. The refund shall be made no longer than 15 (fifteen) working days
after the cancellation date;
4- Other information required by the Director General of the SECC.
Article 23- Unsuccessful Subscription of Debt Securities
The registered disclosure document may be cancelled in case the subscription is not
successful.
Article 24- Report on Result of Debt Securities Offering
The issuer shall submit the report on result of the debt securities offering to qualified
investors to the SECC in accordance with the form determined by the Director General of the
SECC, attached with written letter from the commercial bank which is a cash settlement
agent on the amount of fund in the separate account created for purpose of the offering.
Article 25- Complying with the Procedure at Permitted Securities Market
After completing the issuance process, the issuer may comply with the procedure at
the permitted securities market to list its debt securities for official trading on the permitted
securities market in accordance with enacted Law, Anukret and regulations.
CHAPTER V
POST-ISSUING REQUIREMENTS OF DEBT SECURITIES
Article 26- Compliance with the Prakas on Corporate Disclosure
After issuance of debt securities, the listed entity shall comply with Chapter V of this
Prakas and the Prakas on Corporate Disclosure except Article 6, Article 7, Article 8, Article 9,
Article 21 and Article 23 of the Prakas on Corporate Disclosure.
Article 27- Timely Disclosure
A listed entity shall disclose timely disclosure to investors through permitted securities
market in the form determined by the permitted securities market and send a copy (Carbon
Copy) to the SECC at the same time when any following events occurred:
1- There is any change in the Article of Association of the listed entity;
2- When the listed entity is unable to pay interest and/or principal according to the
debt payment period under the terms and conditions;
3- There is interest payment and/or principle payment;
n
4- There is the decision to delay the coupon payment; o

9- When the listed entity repurchases part or all of its debt securities in the secondary
market;
10- An account of the listed entity at a bank is frozen, or an account is permitted to be
released after having been frozen;
11- Any amendment to the terms and conditions or/and collateral of debt securities,
the listed entity shall submit the related documents to the SECC within 10 (ten)
working days. Such amendment shall be done through bondholders' meeting by
indicating the reason of such amendment and the effect which occurs or may occur
to the bondholders for their decision making;
12- Any material information which can affect the listed entity and/or its credit
worthiness.
If any event as mentioned in the first paragraph occur, except Point 11, listed
entity shall disclose such event to permitted securities market and send a copy (Carbon Copy)
to the SECC at the same time not during trading hour and at least one hour before trading
time of the next day.
Article 28- Periodic Disclosure
A listed entity shall submit annual report to the SECC in the form determined by the
Director General of the SECC within 90 (ninety) days after the end of financial year or other
period determined by the Director General of the SECC. Unless there is an approval from the
Director General of the SECC, an annual report shall contain the following information:
1- General information of a listed entity;
2- Information of the result of business operation including business segments;
3- A statement by the Chairman including the Board’s assessment of future
prospectus for the listed entities;
4- Financial statement audited by the external auditor;
5- Other information necessary to protect investors required by the Directors General
of the SECC.
In order to verify and review of annual report, a listed entity shall submit the report of
management letter to the SECC for internal use within 5 (five) working days after receiving
from the external auditor. The SECC may require the listed entity to explain, submit all
related documents, and/or adjust the financial information. In case where necessary, the
Director General of the SECC may appoint officials to on-site inspection on documents
and/or bookkeeping.
Each submitted report to the SECC shall specify the date, and mention that “read and
approved”, with the signature of chairman of board directors or person authorized to sign on
behalf of the listed entity by attached the power of attorney.
Article 29- Providing of Required Document and On-site Visit by the SECC
Permitted securities market or the Director General of the SECC may require a listed
entity to provide necessary documents and/or may on-site inspection in order to review
corporate information submitted by the listed entity or to strengthen the obligation as
prescribed in this Prakas. For this case, the listed entity shall be well cooperate and provide all
related documents without delay.

Article 31- Obligation to Report on the Change of Bondholders Representative
The listed entity shall get prior approval from the Director General of the SECC on the
change of bondholders representative. And after obtaining approval, the issuer shall submit a
copy of the new bondholders representative agreement to the SECC within 15 (fifteen)
working days from the appointment date.
CHAPTER VI
FEES AND CHARGES
Article 32- Application Fee and Charges for Reviewing Documents for Disclosure
Document Registration
The applicant shall pay 12,000,000 (twelve million) Riels as the application fees and
charges for reviewing and registering the disclosure document when filing application to the
SECC.
Article 33- Charge for Reviewing Documents for Additional and/or Replacement
Disclosure Document Registration
The applicant who proposes to review and register additional and/or replacement
disclosure document shall pay 1,200,000 (one million two hundred thousand) Riels for
reviewing and registering additional and/or replacement disclosure document when making
such proposal to the SECC.
Article 34- Non-Refundable Fees
The fees as mentioned in Article 32 and 33 of this Prakas shall not be refunded even if
the disclosure document is not approved and registered.
CHAPTER VII
PENALTIES
Article 35- Administrative Sanctions
Any person who contravenes any provisions of this Prakas shall receive the following
administrative sanctions:
1- Warning or admonition;
2- Order to submit a memorandum;
3- Public notice of such fact and order to redress;
4- Restriction on the public offering of debt securities;
5- Order to dismiss director(s) or senior officer(s);
6- Public announcement on the actions taken as a result of violation of the applicable
law and regulations;
7- Suspension or prohibition of the public offering or the secondary distribution of debt
securities.

CHAPTER VIII
FINAL PROVISIONS
Article 37- Adoption of Guidelines
The SECC may adopt guidelines to facilitate the understanding and compliance with
the requirements of this Prakas to related parties, securities market participants, and the
public.
Article 38- Abrogation
All provisions contrary to this Prakas are hereby abrogated.
Article 39- Application
The Director General of the SECC, the director of department of Securities Issuance
Supervision, other directors of departments, other Units of the SECC and related parties shall
effectively implement this Prakas from the signing date.
